artworks.title: Laocoön and His Sons
artworks.description: The Vatican Laocoön — snakes crushing the priest who warned against the horse, Virgil's omen of Troy's last night made marble.

artworks.title: Laocoön
artworks.description: El Greco transplants the priest's death to a storm-lit Toledo: the wooden horse and a spectral city watch as Troy's omen becomes apocalypse.

artworks.title: Neoptolemus and Astyanax
artworks.description: Neoptolemus and Astyanax — the sack's most infamous child-killing, Hector's son torn from the walls.

artworks.title: Child Murder (Mykonos Vase, detail)
artworks.description: On the Mykonos vase the horse's belly opens into massacre — among Greece's earliest pictures of Troy's fall.

films.title: Troy
films.description: The wooden horse and the burning city — Petersen's epic made the sack the defining Trojan image for a generation.

popCulture.title: Trojan War
popCulture.description: The night the horse enters and Priam's city falls — the Sack remains the archetype of civilization ending in fire.

popCulture.title: Aeneid
popCulture.creator: Virgil
popCulture.description: Book II is Aeneas' testimony of the sack — Sinon, Laocoön, and the gods withdrawing as Troy dies.
